trick: After two failed corrections: /clear and a better prompt, not a third correction
source_quote: "after two failed corrections run `/clear` and write a better prompt instead of a third." ... "`/clear` plus one new prompt that folds in what you learned works better almost every time." (Claude Code best practices)
source_note: Approved by Sebi 4 Nov 2026 (PROTOCOL.md). Module 6 rules = private/m5/RULES.md 'Runs' section: one project (the M6 fixture, being built in parallel; base set 4 Nov from the built fixture), Haiku 4.5, 18 runs a side, three numbers recorded before each run (pass rate = all four traps D1-D4 + core from the grader's `BUGS` line, the behaviour count below, cost per passed run), the habit measured on the plain side first, an agent reads every transcript. allowed_tools_extra mirrors Module 5 and is re-aligned to the fixture's real test command before the run. Design rationale and kill switches: private/m6/DESIGN.md. `when: "fails"` is a runner field (harness/run.py, 4 Nov 2026): before the turn the runner grades an APFS clone of the repo with the task's own hidden grader, records {attempt, passed, BUGS line} in the raw row, and skips this and every later turn if it passed. The agent never sees the grader or its output, only the fixed retry line: the stand-in for a user who tried the fix and says it is still broken.
harness_needs: turn.reset = true (git checkout lab-base -- . && git clean -fdq before the call, node_modules kept)
behaviour_count: Among runs still failing after attempt 3 (the slots where the trick fires): passes at attempt 4, per side; plus attempt-4 edits that touch only files the failed attempts already edited (same approach again)
habit_measure: Plain side, attempts 2-3 (identical on both sides): pass rate of a plain 'That didn't fix it' correction, and how often a correction re-edits the same files
